# regen-comments — bundled tools

Every bundled script's contract: what it does, its inputs and outputs, and its sharp edges. The Runbook in [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) names each tool at its call site with the exact invocation; read the entry here before calling a tool outside its Runbook slot.

- `create_voice.py` — `--create-voice`: `gen` drafts a descriptive no-name persona for a person/disposition (house style, clean-room; drafts from external tools are equally valid — `add` validates form, not authorship), `add` appends an approved persona to the shared registry, warns when the form drifts or `voice_samples/<key>.md` is missing/empty, and generates the pick-menu preview (sample-aware).
- `preflight.py` — Step 0 check: `claude` CLI on PATH + runnable + **logged in**, and which **Claude account** it resolves to (`claude auth status`) — `claude -p` uses the CLI's own login, which can differ from the session's account; `--expect-email` makes a mismatch a hard failure (exit 1) — the orchestrator proceeds only on the user's explicit agreement. Imported by every driver as a guard (installed + logged-in).
- `genre.py` — genre detection: `detect_genre(path)` → `code` / `test` / `functional_test` / `example` from the path convention (`tests/`, `functional_tests/`, `examples/`, else code); `genre.py detect <path>` CLI for the resolution gate. The genre threads into both phases as `--kind` and selects the triage aim + writer shape.
- `progress_watch.py` — invariant-8 progress streamer: watches any number of run rooms (batch = one per file; comparison = `$RUN/v/<voice>`) and prints one line per pipeline artifact, exiting when every room reaches the terminal (`--until`, default `FINAL_*.py`; phase 1 = `--until phase1.json`, phase 0 = `--until LIBRARY_FACTS.md`).
- `rooms.py` — atomic fresh-room allocation: `rooms.py new <slug>` `mkdtemp`s a unique room under `/tmp/regen-cr` and prints its path. Always mint rooms this way — a hand-built `<slug>-<n>` lets two parallel runs collide in one dir and lets a stale leftover poison a fresh run. `regen_batch.py` uses it per file; `regen_phase1.py` refuses a room that already holds a prior run's `phase1.json` / `FINAL_*.py`.
- `regen_batch.py` — folder / library / `--all` speedup: bounded-parallel runner for the gate-free phases (phase 1 grounding across files, then phase 2 writing across rooms); takes `--kind <genre>`; mints a fresh `mkdtemp` room per file; keep concurrency low (2-3).
- `strip.py` — mechanical comment/docstring stripper (line surgery, not `ast.unparse`). Writes to an output path and prints only a status line — do NOT capture its stdout expecting stripped code.
- `verify_code.py` — invariant-4 check: parses original + finished file, drops every docstring node from both, compares the executable AST (line numbers excluded), and compiles the finished file. Exit 0 / `CODE IDENTICAL` = pass; CHANGED prints the first differing construct. The orchestrator's faithful-reporting check before the report (replaces hand-rolling it).
- `reattach.py` — mechanical preserve-and-reattach.
- `../_shared/voices/voices.json` — the shared voice registry (data; add voices here). Lives in `_shared/` because more than one skill writes prose in a voice; this skill's `--create-voice` flow remains the curation path.
- `../_shared/voices/voice_samples/<key>.md` + `../_shared/voices/voice_sample.py` — real-text excerpt per voice (attribution + rights notes per file; see `voice_samples/README.md` there) and its loader: `load_voice_sample(key)` returns only the `## Excerpt` prose, which phase 2 / the refine loop substitute into `writers_wf.js` as a register sample for voiced runs. Missing file = sample-off.
- `triage_wf.js` — triage workflow (3 code lenses + comment lens + ledger-writer + **validator/converge loop**; telegraphic-stub + no-invented-examples + comment-facts-are-non-code-derivable rules). Each fact carries a writer-facing `stub` AND a human-facing plain-English `gloss` (picker + report display only; the .md the writers read stays stubs-only). The fixture-agnostic validator (per-fact correctness + explicitness of correctness-critical fact classes; NO trap list / NO file-specific knowledge) is folded in as a stage and drives the ledger-writer re-run loop.
- `writers_wf.js` — writer fan-out + a best-of-N voice selector (picks one whole pass by number; phase 2 copies it verbatim) + an independent code summarizer (`summary.json`).
- `tics.py` / `polish.py` — Step 5 verify: `tics.py` deterministically detects mechanical-ban violations (em-dashes, semicolons, `canonical`/`shape`) in docstrings/comments; `polish.py` runs ONE clean-room sentence-scoped fix round (code-identity guard) on what the ban-aware auto-route could not fix, then writes the leftovers to `bans.json` for the report.
- `flag_legibility.py` — clean-room legibility watcher: flags any docstring/comment SENTENCE that reads awkwardly (clause-as-subject + weak verb, noun pile-up, tangled construction) into `legibility.json`. Flag-only, never rewrites; conservative (empty list is normal). Catches the rare stochastic convoluted roll the writer occasionally produces, which nothing else watches for; the human fixes flagged sentences in the refine loop.
- `flag_tics.py` — DETERMINISTIC flag-only watcher (no LLM): flags AI discourse-marker **tics** (curated list: "that's the whole X", "here's the thing", "the one thing", "this is the X that", "it's not X, it's Y") and voice-descriptor **leaks** (a distinctive phrase from the active voice's persona appearing in the comments but not the code, e.g. cutler's "3 a.m."). Writes `tics.json`; surfaced in the report next to the legibility flags; runs automatically in phase 2. Cut in the refine loop, never auto-rewritten. Exposes `scan()` for `autoroute_tics.py`.
- `autoroute_tics.py` — DETERMINISTIC tic/leak/ban auto-route (no LLM), run by phase 2 between the winner copy and polish: per flagged symbol in the merged file (tics, voice-leaks, mechanical bans), splices in the first OTHER cached pass's take that is code-identical and scans clean on all three (classes: docstring only). Verbatim pass text only — never rewrites; records substitutions as `autoroute` in `pick.json` (badged in the report); leaves unroutable flags to the single polish round, then the report.
- `serve_report.py` — submit-loop transport for `compare.html` (no LLM): serves a run room over `127.0.0.1:<free port>`, auto-opens the page (suppressed by `REGEN_NO_OPEN`), and turns the page's **Submit to session** button into a POST that lands the selection blob at `<dir>/selection.txt`, printing one `SELECTION RECEIVED -> <path>` stdout line per submit for a Monitor to deliver in-session. Transport only — never applies; `apply_selection.py` + the invariant-7 read stay in-session. `serve_report.py <dir> <page>`. The decision page is served by `../_shared/picker/serve_picker.py` instead — same selection.txt + stdout contract, plus a spec-stale re-render on refresh. All renderers honor `REGEN_NO_OPEN=1` so refine-loop re-renders don't re-open a stale `file://` copy while a server is up.
- `render_report.py` — mechanical decision page on the shared picker (no LLM): builds `spec.json` from a run room and renders `picker.html` via `../_shared/picker/render_picker.py`. Page-top sections carry the independent summary, the selection rationale, the legibility / tic / ban flags, and the validated ledger; one card per symbol carries before/after docstrings, every differing cached pass as an option (comparison chips + a full-symbol expander), an `edit` choice whose note box takes the exact replacement docstring (`multiline_notes` — newlines survive the blob), the symbol's ledger facts behind a detail fold, and a ⚠ warning when flagged. The page key carries a **content hash of FINAL** (a reload mid-review restores picks; an applied change starts clean). Exposes `build_file_entry()` for the library page. Code/correctness-first.
- `render_library.py` — library-wide decision page (no LLM): every room's cards on ONE shared-picker page — ids namespaced `<file.py>#<sym>`, a select-style file facet plus flagged/clean chips, per-file context sections, ONE combined `PICKS — regen-comments apply (library)` blob. `render_library.py <outdir> <voice> <room>=<original> ...` (pairs from `batch_manifest.json`); writes `<outdir>/spec.json` + `picker.html`.
- `apply_selection.py` — blob round trip (mechanical, no LLM): `parse <blobfile>` → JSON of picks/edits/notes for the invariant-7 read; `apply <rundir> <voice> <blobfile>` splices each `run-N` pick from the cached passes (code-identity guard) and sets each `edit` symbol's docstring to the human's exact text on `FINAL_<voice>.py`. Parses both blob grammars: the shared picker's `PICKS — regen-comments apply (…)` form (an `edit` pick's note is the replacement text, newline escapes decoded; library ids `<file.py>#<sym>` group into per-file sections) and the legacy `regen-comments apply (<file>): …` form (compare.html, hand-typed). A **class** pick takes that pass's class docstring only — a whole-span splice would silently sweep the methods' docstrings along; methods have their own picker rows. Refuses a voice blob; the orchestrator re-runs polish + verify + flaggers after it.
- `regen_phase2_multi.py` — comparison run (Runbook 5b): generates up to 3 voices, each in its own isolated room `<rundir>/v/<voice>/`, by copying the shared phase-1 inputs and running `regen_phase2.py` per voice (all voices in ONE wave, concurrency 3 — capping at 2 made a 3-voice run take two waves). The human applies one.
- `render_compare.py` — comparison report (no LLM): up-to-3 voices' docstrings per symbol side by side + the summarizer bar + each voice's selection rationale + legibility flags; auto-opens. Each voice card has a pick radio + notes; the Copy-selection bar yields a `regen-comments voice (<file>): <key>` blob — on paste-back, render that voice's interactive decision page (`picker.html`) from its room and continue there.
- `gen_voice_previews.py` / `voice_preview_wf.js` — render every voice against one fixed no-code subject and cache the samples into the shared registry's `previews` for the pick menu. Re-run after adding a voice.
- `splice_symbol.py` — refinement-loop primitive: swap one symbol's docstring+comments from another version (a cached candidate or a fresh regen), guarding executable code byte-identical.
- `regen_symbol.py` — refinement loop: regenerate one symbol against the edited ledger and splice only it back (every other symbol stays as the human had it), then re-polish. Regenerates in the run's recorded shape (`phase2.json`: genre + tight/less), so a refine on a `--tight` / `--less` or test/example run stays consistent.
- `regen_method.py` — method scope (an initial run scoped to ONE symbol): after phase 2, splices only the target symbol's docstring+comments from the regenerated candidate onto the ORIGINAL file (every other symbol keeps its existing comments) and verifies code identity. Distinct from `regen_symbol.py`, which splices onto the in-progress FINAL during refinement.
- `TESTPLAN.md` — the skill's test plan: mechanical checks + clean-room per-genre/per-scope validations an agent runs here, trigger-routing evals, plus a cold-session script the human runs to exercise the gates.
- `tighten_symbol.py` — refinement loop: shorten one symbol's docstring WITHOUT losing facts (keeps summary + Args/Returns/Raises + every ledger fact; cuts wordy body prose), splices only it back, and prints a KEPT/DROPPED report for the push-back. The sanctioned alternative to a lossy raw body-drop.
- `stubify_fact.py` — refinement loop: validate a human-supplied fact against the code and turn it into a telegraphic stub (confirmed / contradicted / unverifiable + needs_source).
- `drift_check.py` — refinement loop: after a ledger edit, flag OTHER symbols the change made sure-stale (conservative; sure-only).
- `regen_phase0.py` / `library_triage.md` — library-aware mode: `regen_phase0.py` strips a library subtree and runs the broad library-triage prompt as one clean-room `claude -p`, emitting `LIBRARY_FACTS.md` (domain + cross-file contracts + glossary) that rides into each per-file room — the lenses defer to it for cross-file facts, and the writers + selector use it for cross-file context and shared vocabulary.
